newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Birch says forecasts assume end-'96 easing.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Birch says forecasts assume end-'96 easing.

text.p: New Zealand caretaker Finance Minister Bill Birch said on Monday that the latest set of Treasury forecasts assumed an easing of monetary policy towards the end of 1996.
"The forecasts are based on a loosening of monetary policy towards the end of 1996. That's the sort of expectation held by the bank itself," Birch said, referring to the central Reserve Bank.

"Really you've got to look at what the bank has been saying. The bank itself makes a decision about loosening or tightening monetary policy, and we've picked up the expectations of the bank, the signals that it's put out, and that's been built into these forecasts," he told a news conference.
